action_trace.summary: Generated 10 targeted interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (abstract class design rationale, workflow enablement), pain points (fit() groups parameter, current implementation limitations), and acceptance criteria (success metrics, constraints). Questions decompose the SequentialFeatureSelector requirement across problem space, stakeholder context, and solution trade-offs to drive iterative requirements refinement per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and BABOK v3 standards.

Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (workflow enablement, abstract class rationale), pain points (current implementation gaps, grouped evaluation needs), and acceptance criteria (success measures, interface requirements, edge cases) for SequentialFeatureSelector enhancement with fit() groups parameter support.

Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (abstract class for SequentialFeatureSelector), pain points (current implementation gaps), and acceptance criteria (success definition, constraints). Questions decompose the requirement fragment into actionable discovery topics: workflow enablement, pain-point validation, stakeholder identification, integration points, timeline, success metrics, alternative analysis, and trade-off reasoning aligned with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 and BABOK v3 standards.

End-user requires abstract selector base class and SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter support to enable automated, group-aware feature selection in production ML pipelines while maintaining sklearn API consistency.

End-user confirms two critical pain points: (1) manual feature selection inefficiency in high-dimensional ML pipelines, and (2) SequentialFeatureSelector's inability to handle grouped data scenarios causing data leakage risk. Expects standardized abstract base class for seamless selector interchangeability and groups parameter support in fit() method for time-series and stratified workflows. Usage scenarios validate need for group-aware feature evaluation in financial time-series and imbalanced classification contexts.

End-user feedback prioritizes solving manual feature selection bottlenecks (30-40% pipeline time) and adding group parameter support to SequentialFeatureSelector to prevent data leakage in grouped/time-series scenarios. Abstract base class standardization is expected to improve ecosystem consistency and enable reproducible, production-ready feature engineering workflows.

Clarification needed on: (1) scope and design of abstract feature selector base class; (2) groups parameter semantics and enforcement in SequentialFeatureSelector; (3) per-group vs. aggregated metric computation; (4) specific CV strategies to support; (5) relationship between base class and groups parameter implementation; and (6) concrete examples of current workaround pain points.

End-user raises six clarification questions addressing scope ambiguity (abstract base class coverage), technical implementation details (groups parameter convention and enforcement), aggregation strategy decisions for grouped metrics, interface flexibility, data leakage prevention in time-series scenarios, and performance considerations. These questions bridge the gap between high-level pain points (manual feature selection burden, missing group support) and concrete design decisions needed for sklearn implementation.

Seven clarification questions raised to resolve ambiguities around abstract base class scope, groups parameter semantics, metric aggregation strategy, backward compatibility, validation logic, and data leakage prevention in grouped feature selection workflows.

End user confirms need for abstract base class (sequential selectors focus, backward compatible) and SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter (CV convention, per-group metrics with mean aggregation, consistency validation). Priority: groups parameter for time-series workflows, then standardization. Requires clarification on groups requirement scope across selector types.

End-user requirements validated and refined: abstract base class for feature selectors will standardize sklearn interface with focus on sequential selectors; SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() groups parameter will follow sklearn CV convention with per-group metric computation and mean aggregation; group consistency validation required across fit/transform; implementation addresses 30-40% time reduction goal in grouped data feature selection workflows.

End-user requirements validated across three dimensions: (1) Abstract base class for sequential feature selectors with backward compatibility maintained, (2) SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() groups parameter implemented per sklearn cross-validation convention with per-group metric computation and mean aggregation, (3) Error handling for group consistency validation between fit/transform lifecycle. All pain points addressed: manual feature selection overhead reduced through standardized interface; grouped data scenarios now supported with data leakage prevention.

Consolidated 7 structured elicitation records from EndUser dialogue (sklearn_2021q4 case): 4 functional requirements (abstract base class, groups parameter, metric aggregation, backward compatibility), 2 problem statements (manual feature selection overhead, grouped data leakage), and 1 operating environment context. All records validated through EndUser confirmations; requirements follow ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 standards with MoSCoW prioritization. Chain-of-Thought decomposition: identified core pain points (time consumption, data leakage) → mapped to desired workflows (automated selection, group-aware evaluation) → formalized as testable functional/non-functional requirements with success criteria.

Nine prioritized user requirements synthesized from interview records, enduser confirmations, and pain point analysis. Core MUST requirements establish abstract base class for feature selectors with standardized interface, SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() groups parameter following sklearn conventions, per-group metrics aggregation via mean strategy, and backward compatibility guardrails. SHOULD requirements address overhead reduction and future extensibility. Chain-of-Thought reasoning: (1) Identified four confirmed MUST requirements from IR records and enduser validations, (2) Derived MUST-005 from unresolved enduser question regarding group validation, (3) Mapped SHOULD priorities to pain points and architectural flexibility, (4) Classified aggregation configurability as WON'T for initial release per confirmed refinement.

Deployer-focused dialogue probing infrastructure constraints (deployment environments, memory/compute limits), security mandates (group label handling, audit requirements), scalability expectations (performance targets, distributed processing needs), backward compatibility deployment strategy, group label validation governance, and testing infrastructure for grouped feature selection validation.

Targeted Deployer dialogue probing six critical dimensions: deployment infrastructure constraints and timelines; security/compliance mandates for grouped data handling; scalability expectations for feature counts and group sizes; CI/CD and backward compatibility validation infrastructure; post-deployment monitoring and ecosystem adoption; and release strategy for coordinating abstract base class and groups parameter rollout across sklearn versions.

Deployer dialogue probes seven critical dimensions: infrastructure deployment targets and SLAs; security/compliance constraints for group label handling; scalability trade-offs for large-scale grouped aggregation; sklearn ecosystem integration requirements; backward compatibility versioning strategy; production validation gates; and observability instrumentation for grouped feature selection workflows.

Deployer confirms infrastructure readiness for sklearn 2021q4 feature selector enhancements: containerized CI/CD across Python 3.8-3.11, <100ms per-group metric computation scaling to 100K samples, strict security validation of group labels with deprecation-cycle backward compatibility, and operational logging for grouped data leakage prevention in time-series scenarios. No new infrastructure investment required; deployment targets 99.5% availability with graceful fallback semantics.

Deployer constraints address Python 3.8-3.11 cross-platform CI/CD with Docker, sub-100ms per-group metric computation via joblib parallelization, strict type/bounds validation for group labels, backward compatibility enforcement, and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 deployment checklist compliance. Security mandates array-like validation and immutability; scalability requires O(n_groups) aggregation; operations prioritize error clarity and cost-efficient parallelization.

Deployer confirms infrastructure (Python 3.8-3.11, Docker CI/CD, joblib parallelization), security (array-like validation, bounds checking, group consistency verification), scalability (<100ms per-group computation, linear group aggregation, <10% memory overhead), and operational constraints (backward compatibility, diagnostic logging, error handling) to enable safe production deployment of abstract base class and SequentialFeatureSelector.fit(groups) enhancement without additional cloud infrastructure costs.

These gaps prevent precise implementation constraints and deployment resource planning for abstract base class and SequentialFeatureSelector.fit(groups) feature.

Deployer raises 5 clarification questions on infrastructure performance budgeting (serialization overhead inclusion), security scope (pandas compatibility in type validation), backward compatibility boundaries (which signatures lock vs. extend), deployment validation gates (performance enforcement in CI/CD), and cost-performance trade-offs (parallelization activation thresholds). These clarifications resolve ambiguities in INFRASTRUCTURE-002, SECURITY-001, and MUST-004 that impact implementation feasibility and operational cost.

Six clarifications requested on performance budgeting methodology, type validation boundaries, backward compatibility scope, consistency validation timing, scalability target applicability, and security validation strategy. These operational context gaps must be resolved before infrastructure provisioning and implementation can proceed without risk of costly rework or breaking changes to existing sklearn selector APIs.

Deployer role validates infrastructure, security, and backward compatibility constraints for sklearn feature selector standardization (abstract base class + SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() groups parameter). Key refinements: clarify joblib serialization budget impact on <100ms per-group metric constraint; implement strict group label type validation with conversion rejection; protect public method signatures while extending internal interface; deploy dynamic parallelization threshold for cost-performance optimization; enforce group consistency across fit/transform lifecycle with cached state tracking. All MUST requirements confirmed viable within deployment environment; SHOULD-001 manual feature selection overhead reduction enabled by standardized grouped feature evaluation workflow.

Deployer confirms deployment readiness for abstract base class and SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() groups parameter across sklearn ecosystem. Infrastructure constraints (<100ms per-group metric computation, joblib parallelization) are achievable; security validation enforces array-like group label compliance; backward compatibility maintained through immutable public signatures. Grouped feature evaluation uses mean aggregation strategy (non-configurable initially). Pain point mitigation validated: manual feature selection overhead reduction and grouped data leakage prevention enable reproducible time-series and stratified scenarios. Recommend clarification on serialization overhead measurement methodology for CI/CD performance gates.

Deployer confirms deployment readiness for abstract base class (IR-001) and SequentialFeatureSelector.fit(groups=...) (IR-002) across infrastructure, security, and scalability dimensions. Key validations: (1) backward compatibility maintained via optional groups parameter; (2) <100ms per-group metric computation achievable with joblib parallelization for 100K×10K datasets; (3) strict array-like type validation prevents cross-validation semantic drift; (4) CI/CD infrastructure supports Python 3.8-3.11 across Linux/macOS/Windows. Deployment proceeds with configuration flexibility (n_jobs parameter) for cost-performance optimization in resource-constrained environments.

Operating environment specification for sklearn feature selector enhancements (abstract base class + SequentialFeatureSelector.fit() groups parameter) requires Python 3.8-3.11 runtime across Linux/macOS/Windows with Docker CI/CD containerization; enforces <100ms per-group metric computation via joblib parallelization for 100K×10K datasets; implements strict array-like type validation and consistency checking on group labels; maintains backward compatibility of public method signatures; uses mean aggregation strategy for grouped metrics without configurability in initial release.

System Requirements List (IEEE 830 format) consolidates 10 requirements from sklearn_2021q4 iReDev workflow: 4 functional requirements (abstract base class, groups parameter, per-group metrics, validation/error handling), 5 non-functional requirements (backward compatibility, runtime environment, performance <100ms, memory isolation, group immutability), and 1 SHOULD requirement (reduce manual overhead). Requirements satisfy all user confirmations, deployer validations, and operating environment constraints while maintaining consistency with sklearn conventions and cross-validation semantics.

Selected SysML Block Definition Diagram + Internal Block Diagram for sklearn_2021q4 requirements modeling. Rationale: SysML captures hierarchical abstraction (abstract base class standardizing feature selector ecosystem), data flow constraints (per-group metric computation with joblib parallelization, validation gates), and non-functional requirements (backward compatibility, security) better than UML Use Case Diagram. SysML constraint blocks explicitly model performance budgets (<100ms), type validation (array-like enforcement), and group label consistency validation critical to deployer concerns. Enables direct traceability from interview records (IR-001 through IR-006) to system requirements (SR-001 through SR-006) per IEEE 830 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 standards.

Requirements model constructed for sklearn_2021q4 feature selector ecosystem standardization. Core model: BaseFeatureSelector abstract class with standardized interface (fit, transform, get_support) enabling backward-compatible integration of SequentialFeatureSelector.fit(groups=None) parameter, per-group metric aggregation (mean strategy), and strict group label validation (numpy/list only, consistent across fit/transform). Identified conflicts: performance vs. compatibility (deferred configurable aggregation to future); gaps: serialization budget ambiguity (clarified as algorithmic time only), pandas type validation boundary (strict rejection with conversion guidance). All six MUST-priority requirements traced and validated for consistency; quality attributes (backward compatibility, runtime support, security, performance) operationalized through specific implementation constraints and validation gates.
